title: Sort Numbers: how it works, formula and examples

content:
The [Sort Numbers](/sort-numbers) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Sort a list of numbers into ascending or descending order. Enter your numbers (comma or space separated) and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Sort a list of numbers into ascending or descending order. Paste numbers separated by commas, spaces or line breaks and get both orders at once, with the count and the range. It is useful for ranking scores, ordering measurements, finding the smallest and largest values, and tidying data before pasting it somewhere else. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Sort Numbers

Start by typing or pasting your numbers (comma or space separated). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Type or paste your numbers, separated by commas, spaces or new lines.
2. Read the ascending list — the headline result.
3. Copy the descending list if you need the largest first.

## Formula

Numbers are ordered by numeric value — not alphabetically, so 100 comes after 42, not before it.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Sort Numbers](/sort-numbers) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. 42, 7, 19, 3, 25 sorted ascending is 3, 7, 19, 25, 42. Descending is 42, 25, 19, 7, 3. Try the same figures in the [Sort Numbers](/sort-numbers) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Numbers (comma or space separated): 42, 7, 19, 3, 25), the [Sort Numbers](/sort-numbers) returns Sorted (ascending): 3, 7, 19, 25, 42, Sorted (descending): 42, 25, 19, 7, 3, Count: 5, Smallest → largest: 3 → 42. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Percentage Calculator](/percentage-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Numeric order, not alphabetical order

Sorting numbers as text gives the wrong answer: alphabetically, 100 comes before 42 because '1' comes before '4'. This tool compares numbers by value, so 3, 7, 19, 25, 42 is the true ascending order. That is the mistake to watch for when sorting in a spreadsheet too — make sure the column is formatted as numbers, not text.

## Finding extremes

A sorted list makes the smallest and largest values obvious, and it also shows gaps and clusters at a glance. If the largest value is far from the rest, it may be an outlier or a typo — worth checking before you use the data further.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Paste straight from a spreadsheet column — new lines work as separators.
- Decimals and negative numbers sort correctly too.
- For the full picture (mean, median, mode), use the Average Calculator.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I sort numbers in ascending order?

Paste them here separated by commas or spaces and read the ascending list. It orders by numeric value, so 100 correctly comes after 42. Try it with your own numbers in the [Sort Numbers](/sort-numbers) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Can I sort decimals and negative numbers?

Yes — decimals, negatives and large numbers all sort by value. Try it with your own numbers in the [Sort Numbers](/sort-numbers) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What is the difference between sorting and ranking?

Sorting orders the values themselves; ranking assigns each value a position (1st, 2nd, 3rd). A sorted list makes ranking easy to read off. Try it with your own numbers in the [Sort Numbers](/sort-numbers) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Sort Numbers use?

Numbers are ordered by numeric value — not alphabetically, so 100 comes after 42, not before it. You can see it in action in the [Sort Numbers](/sort-numbers) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.
